title: The Weight of Silent Choices
text:
Every day, professionals face decisions in which the right course of action is far from obvious. A doctor may have to decide whether to disclose a diagnosis that could distress a patient, while a journalist must weigh the public's right to know against the risk of harming innocent people. Such dilemmas rarely come with clear rules, which is why many ethical frameworks emphasise judgement as much as principle.

Critics argue that responsibility cannot be delegated to a set of guidelines, since those guidelines are themselves written by people with particular interests. Consequently, some organisations now require staff to explain publicly how they reached difficult decisions. Supporters of this practice contend that transparency encourages accountability, although others warn that it may encourage defensive behaviour rather than genuine reflection.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what may a doctor have to decide?
options: whether to tell a patient about a distressing diagnosis
whether to publish a news story

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do some organisations now require their staff to do?
options: explain publicly how they reached difficult decisions

questions.text: What does the author imply about ethical guidelines?
options: They cannot fully remove the need for personal judgement.
They are always written by neutral experts.

questions.text: Why might public transparency have an unintended effect, according to the passage?
options: It may lead to defensive behaviour instead of real reflection.
It makes staff ignore the public completely.
It removes all forms of accountability.
It prevents journalists from reporting the news.

vocabulary.definition: situations where every available choice has significant drawbacks
the obligation to explain and take responsibility for one's actions
acting to protect oneself from criticism rather than to solve a problem

paragraph_translations: Todos os dias, os profissionais enfrentam decisões nas quais o melhor curso de ação está longe de ser óbvio. Um médico pode ter de decidir se revela um diagnóstico que poderia angustiar o paciente, enquanto um jornalista precisa ponderar o direito do público de saber contra o risco de prejudicar pessoas inocentes. Esses dilemas raramente vêm com regras claras, e é por isso que muitos quadros éticos valorizam o julgamento tanto quanto os princípios.

Críticos argumentam que a responsabilidade não pode ser delegada a um conjunto de diretrizes, já que essas diretrizes são, por sua vez, escritas por pessoas com interesses particulares. Consequentemente, algumas organizações agora exigem que os funcionários expliquem publicamente como chegaram a decisões difíceis. Os defensores dessa prática sustentam que a transparência estimula a responsabilização, embora outros alertem que ela pode estimular um comportamento defensivo em vez de uma reflexão genuína.
